What is it to me whether the will of God be presented to me in tribulation or consolation, since I desire and seek only the divine will”( St Francis de Sales) “Jwill attempt day by day to break my will into little pieces. I want to do God holy will not my own(St Rita) ALITTLE THEOLOGY ‘JUDGING OTHERS’ The church teaching distinguishes between judging a person's soul or inner motives-which belong to God alone-and discerning objective mortal actions, which catholic are called to do with humility and charity. The inner intentions, consciences and the full circumstances affecting moral culpability are known to God alone. Presuming to condemn someone or decide their eternal fate violates charity and oversteps human authority. Catholics must still recognise right and wrong and evaluate behaviour. The catechism of the catholic church prohibits rash judgement, assuming another person's moral fault without sufficient grounds. ADVENT WREATH. There is only one week remaining until the start of the Advent season, the 4 weeks leading up to the feast of Christmas, over those 4 weeks every church will be adorned with an Advent wreath. Why not make your own Advent wreath, all you need are some evergreens, some red berries, a simple circular disc of ring, along with these you will need 5 candles 3 purple, one pink and one white. These Advent candle sets are available in most supermarkets. They will be blessed on the first weekend of Advent masses. To give the feast its correct title ‘ The feast of our lord Jesus Christ, king of the universe’, the feast emphasises the true kingship of Christ, and was established as a feast day by pope Pius XI in 1925, following the first World War, the rise of atheistic communionism. At first the feast was celebrated on the last Sunday in October, Pope Paul moved it to its present date, the last Sunday of the churches year, he did this in order to point to the end times and Christ's return as ruler & master of all things. We remember them. At the blowing of the wind and in the chill of winter.
We remember them. At the opening of the buds and in the rebirth of spring.
We remember them. At the blueness of the skies and in the warmth of summer.
We remember them. At the rustling of the leaves and in the beauty of autumn.
We remember them. At the beginning of the year and when it ends.
We remember them. When we are weary and in need of strength.
We remember them. When we are lost and sick at heart.
We remember them. When we have joy, we crave to share.
We remember them. When we have decisions that are difficult to make.
We remember them. When we have achievements that are based on theirs.
We remember them. As long as we live, they too will live, for they are now a part of us.
